newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kansai Elec study paves way for new power plant.
newsitem.headline: Kansai Elec study paves way for new power plant.

text.p: Kansai Electric Power Co Inc said on Tuesday that it had obtained favourable results from an environmental study, paving the way for the construction of a 3.7 million-kilowatt power plant in western Japan.
"We have obtained good results from our research on the possible impact of a power plant on the environment and we have reported it to the government," a company spokesman said.

The company hopes to build a liquified natural gas power plant in Wakayaka Prefecture with a production capacity of 3.7 million kilowatts of electricity, the spokesman said. The company hopes to start partial operations in November 2004, he said.
"It usually costs about one trillion yen to build a power plant of this size although we do not yet know what the exact cost of our plant will be," he said.
He said the company had yet to decide where the company would buy LNG for the plant.
